title: Weyl's lemma on a ball: a distributionally harmonic L¹ function is a.e. equal to a smooth harmonic function
statement: Let n ≥ 1, R > 0, and let W : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) be integrable on B := B̆_R(0). Suppose ∫_B W·Δζ = 0 for every ζ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C² with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ B, where Δζ(y) = Σ_i iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 ζ y ![e_i, e_i] and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then there is h : ℝⁿ → ℝ which is C^m on B for every m ∈ ℕ, satisfies Σ_i iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![e_i, e_i] = 0 at every y ∈ B, and agrees with W Lⁿ-almost everywhere on B.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (W : Euclid n → ℝ), 0 < n → 0 < R → IntegrableOn W (ball (0 : Euclid n) R) → (∀ ζ : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 2 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball (0 : Euclid n) R → ∫ y in ball (0 : Euclid n) R, W y * ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 ζ y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0) → ∃ h : Euclid n → ℝ, (∀ m : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ m h (ball (0 : Euclid n) R)) ∧ (∀ y ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) R, ∑ i : Fin n, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 h y ![EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ), EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)] = 0) ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume.restrict (ball (0 : Euclid n) R)), h y = W y
